newsitem.title: UK: Analysts downgrade MFI profit forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Analysts downgrade MFI profit forecasts.

text.p: Results from British furniture retailer MFI Furniture Group Plc on Tuesday prompted some retail analysts to downgrade profit forecasts for the current year.

Analysts, who were cutting their forecasts, said heavy investment this year could limit profit growth and the full impact of cost savings from the investment would not come through until the following year.
They reduced their profit forecasts to between 75 and 85 million stg from 82 to 90 million.
"Costs are rising and the sales line is not that strong," said one.

Other sector analysts said the market's dissatisfaction with the current sales performance was an overreaction and sales were on an uptrend after deteriorating in the second half of the past financial year.
"The shares look undervalued unless the consumer gets hammered in the budget," said another analyst, referring to the Labour government's first budget on Wednesday.
They said the company had seen a very substantial uplift in kitchen plans, 60 percent of which translate into actual sales.

John Richards, retail analyst at NatWest Markets, said investment in the stores and manufacturing would peak this year and there would be "very significant" cost savings from MFI's new distribution programme. He said he was holding his forecast at 90 million stg.
MFI's shares were 6.5 pence lower at 128.5 by 1340 GMT.
